idiom_name: EF Core DbContext identity resolution (change tracker)
implementation_notes: EF Core's DbContext is the identity map: it can track only one entity instance per primary-key value, so a query or FindAsync returns the already-tracked instance instead of materialising a second one, and attaching another instance with the same key throws InvalidOperationException ('another instance with the key value is already being tracked'). The classic keyed map is therefore replaced by context lifetime - one context per unit of work or request - and by query-then-apply-changes (PropertyValues.SetValues) instead of attaching DTO-shaped copies. Prefer the framework context over a hand-written Dictionary; a manual map is only justified in plain ADO.NET code without EF.
pitfalls: A long-lived DbContext keeps every loaded entity alive and serves stale values - the map's lifetime is the context's lifetime, so use one per unit of work.
Attaching a second instance with the same key (deserialised graph, retry, reused context) throws; merge into the tracked instance or Find it first.
DbContext is not thread-safe: concurrent operations need separate contexts, and parallel queries on one context are a classic production bug.
